msg: No YAML frontmatter block. A Hugging Face model card must open with a --- block; without it the Hub stores no licence, no task and no dataset link, and EU AI Act Annex XII information for downstream providers has nowhere to live. Add a --- block as line 1.

Frontmatter has no license: key. The Hub refuses to show a licence it was not told, and a downstream provider cannot accept your model without one (AI Act Annex XII). Write license: apache-2.0 (or the SPDX id that applies).
license: other is declared without license_name and license_link. 'other' is the one value the Hub cannot resolve on its own. Add both keys so the terms are readable.
Frontmatter has no pipeline_tag:. Without it the model is missing from task search and gets no inference widget. Write pipeline_tag: text-generation (or the task that applies).
Frontmatter has no library_name:. The Hub then guesses how to load the model and the usage snippet on the page can be wrong. Write library_name: transformers.

Frontmatter has no language:. Language is part of the intended-use statement a deployer needs (AI Act Annex XII) and it is how the model is filtered on the Hub. Write language: en (list every language).

Frontmatter has no datasets: key. Training-data provenance is the first thing an EU AI Act Art. 53(1)(d) reviewer looks for and the first thing an enterprise buyer asks for. List the dataset ids, or say in the body why they cannot be listed.
Frontmatter has no tags:. Tags are how the model is found on the Hub at all. Add at least the task, the domain and the base architecture.

Frontmatter has no model-index:. Without it the numbers in your Evaluation section are prose, not results the Hub can display or a buyer can compare. Add a model-index block with the metric, the dataset and the value.

'[More Information Needed]' is still in the card. That is the Hugging Face template's own placeholder: this section was never written. Every one of these is a documentation gap an auditor can point at.
An unrendered template expression is still in the card. The card was generated from a template and never filled in, so the text on the page is not about this model.
A TODO/TBD marker is still in the card. Published model cards are read by procurement and by regulators; an open marker reads as an admission that the section is unfinished.
A placeholder from the template is still in the card. Replace it with the real name, the real repository or the real contact before this page is quoted anywhere.
This heading has no text under it — the next line is another heading. An empty section is the same gap as a missing one, but it looks answered.

any: public summary of the content used for training
msg: No public summary of training content. EU AI Act Art. 53(1)(d) requires a provider of a general-purpose AI model to publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used for training, on the Commission's template. Add a 'Training Data Summary' section that links it.

No copyright policy is stated. EU AI Act Art. 53(1)(c) requires a policy to comply with Union copyright law, including honouring machine-readable rights reservations (TDM opt-outs). One paragraph saying what you crawled, and what you honoured, is the whole duty.
The card names no provider and no contact. Annex XII asks for the identity of the provider of the model; a downstream deployer with a question about your model has nobody to write to.

No intended-use section. This is the single sentence that decides whether a deployer may put your model into a high-risk system at all, and Annex XII expects it. Write what the model is for, in one paragraph.
No out-of-scope section. Saying what the model must not be used for is how a provider limits its own exposure and how a deployer knows where the line is. Name at least the uses you refuse.
No evaluation section. Annex XI expects the evaluation strategies and results to be documented. A number with the dataset and the metric beside it is worth more than a paragraph of description.
No limitations or bias section. Annex XI expects known limitations to be documented, and this is the section enterprise review reads first. Name the failure modes you already know about.
No energy consumption figure. Annex XI expects the known or estimated energy consumption of the model. An estimate with the method beside it satisfies this; silence does not.

No training compute figure. Annex XI expects the computational resources used for training. It is also the number that decides Art. 51 systemic-risk classification, where training compute above 10^25 FLOP is presumed to be systemic risk — you cannot show you are under a threshold you never stated.

No authorised representative is named. EU AI Act Art. 54 requires a provider established outside the Union to appoint an authorised representative in the Union before placing a general-purpose AI model on the EU market. If you are established in the Union, say so in one line and this stops applying.

The card gives no placing-on-the-market date. It decides which clock you are on: models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 have until 2 August 2027 to meet the Art. 53 duties, everything after is already due. One dated line settles it.

pattern: (fine-?tun|derived from|based on the|continued pre-?train|distilled from|merge of)
msg: The text says this model is derived from another one, but frontmatter has no base_model:. The Hub then shows no lineage, and Annex XII information from the upstream provider is not linked to yours. Add base_model: org/name.

A base_model is declared but the card never says what the upstream licence permits. A restrictive base licence travels to your weights whatever your own license: key says. State in one line which terms you inherited.

The card dates itself to a year that has already passed. A model card that still says 'as of' an earlier year tells a buyer the documentation stopped being maintained — and under Art. 53 the documentation has to be kept up to date.
